metadata.hardware_requirements: Server ('computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)')

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volumes and video data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, collected from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data is available upon request from the corresponding author; no direct URL or public repository is provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Set up the road network in SUMO based on empirical data from the Qingdao-Huangdao freeway. Simulate traffic from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. to generate traffic video frames and measurements.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, tool named, simulation times stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed... After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4 x 512 in pixels.
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle locations from raw images. Zoom, down-sample, and stack three consecutive frames to form a state matrix of size 3x4x512 representing the traffic state.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, parameters stated, generic tools required but no specific library named

nodes_process.source_quote: consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Initialize a deep Q-network with 3 CNN layers and 2 FC layers for multitask learning, predicting Q-value, speed, and queue length simultaneously.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, architecture detailed in text and Fig 7, no specific deep learning framework named

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames... The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update wi to minimize the loss function.
nodes_process.description: Train the Q-network using experience replay, a target network, and the Adam optimizer over 4200 training steps.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all hyperparameters explicitly listed in Table 1, optimizer named

nodes_process.source_quote: KR = 90 and KP = 50 are two regulator parameters in PI-ALINEA, which are fine-tuned to minimize mean travel times in the traffic system.
nodes_process.description: Implement the PI-ALINEA ramp metering method as a baseline, fine-tuning regulator parameters KR and KP to minimize mean travel times.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, mathematical formulation and all parameters provided

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_process.description: Evaluate the trained DRL model, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios in 20 simulation experiments. Compare travel times, speeds, queue lengths, and downstream volumes.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, evaluation protocol and number of runs clearly stated

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: Divide the control area into eight subareas and remove information from each subarea to generate perturbed data, evaluating the impact on travel time.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, perturbation method clearly described with subarea count

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves for episode reward and mean travel time during the training process of the deep Q-network.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training hyperparameters and architecture are specified, but the underlying code and empirical traffic data are not publicly available, limiting independent reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Vehicle travel times in the mainline across three scenarios: no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation setup in SUMO is described, but the exact empirical data used for calibration and the source code are not provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Results are derived from 20 SUMO simulations with different random seeds. Lack of open code and data restricts full reproducibility.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualizes simulation outputs. Depends on SUMO setup and proprietary empirical data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length at the on-ramp over time for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear aggregation of simulation outputs, but underlying data and code are not public.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Scatter plots of simulation metrics. Reproducibility limited by closed source data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length and occupancy over time for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Time series of simulation metrics. Reproducibility limited by closed source data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Downstream volume in three scenarios (No control, PI-ALINEA, Deep RL) over time.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Box plots of downstream volumes from simulations. Reproducibility limited by closed source data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Travel time with perturbed input data, showing the impact of removing information from different subareas.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation analysis results. Clear methodology but relies on closed simulation setup and data.
